## Appendix F. A fixed catalogue for the conserved families

Throughout, a cyclic digraph has three vertex classes, and every arc goes from
class i to class i+1 modulo 3. Digraphs have no repeated arcs. The degree d(v)
means **in-degree plus out-degree**. A signed circulation is an integer vector
on the arcs with equal incoming and outgoing sums at every vertex. A positive
piece is a nonempty set of arcs which is balanced in the same sense. It need not
be a single cycle. Its size is its number of arcs.

For a finite catalogue C of pieces, its load at v is

$$
\operatorname{load}_{\mathcal C}(v)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal C}d_P(v).
$$

This counts the entire catalogue, not merely the pieces selected for a
particular residual graph. All reserves and catalogues below are chosen before
the residual L. Only the partition selected from the catalogue depends on L.

### F.1. Integer rounding and a two-sided inverse

Orient the edges of a finite simple graph arbitrarily and let B be its signed
incidence matrix, with a column $e_{v}-e_{u}$ for an edge oriented from u to v.

**Flow rounding.** If Bf is integral, there is an integral vector z with $Bz=Bf$
and $\lfloor f_e\rfloor\le z_e\le\lceil f_e\rceil$ for every edge e. In particular $|z_{e}-f_{e}|<1$.

To see this, consider the edges on which f is not integral. No vertex has exactly
one such incident edge: its incidence equation would have a nonintegral left
side and an integral right side. If any such edge remains, their underlying
graph therefore contains a cycle. Add a signed multiple of its cyclic incidence
vector. This preserves Bf. Increase the multiple until an edge first reaches an
integer endpoint of its allowed interval. No other coordinate leaves its
interval, and at least one nonintegral coordinate disappears. Previously
integral coordinates are not changed. Iteration terminates, proving the claim.

Suppose G satisfies the cut inequality

$$
|\partial_G S|\ge h\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\},\qquad h>0.\tag{F.1}
$$

Every zero-sum real vector g with $|g_{v}|\le M$ has a real preimage under B of
supremum norm at most M/h. Indeed,

$$
\left|\sum_{v\in S}g_v\right|\le M\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\}\le(M/h)|\partial_G S|.
$$

These cut inequalities imply the flow assertion. For completeness, the image
of the box $[-M/h,M/h]^E$ under B is a compact convex set. If g were outside it,
a separating potential p would satisfy

$$
\langle p,g\rangle>(M/h)\sum_{uv\in E}|p_u-p_v|.
$$

Subtract a constant from p, which does not change the left side, and express p
as a sum of indicators of its nested level sets multiplied by consecutive
level differences. Apply the cut inequality to each term and sum. This gives
the reverse inequality, a contradiction. Integral g can then be rounded as
above without changing its divergence.

**Two-sided inverse.** Let A and B be connected graphs with expansion constants
$h_{A},h_{B}$. If X is an integral matrix with zero row and column sums and
$|X_{ab}|\le M$, then

$$
B_A Z B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |Z_{ef}|<\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}+2.\tag{F.2}
$$

for an integral matrix Z.

First lift each column of X through $B_{A}$, obtaining columns $u_{b}$ bounded by
$M/h_{A}$. Set $s_b=u_b-\operatorname{mean}_{b\prime}u_{b\prime}$. Then $B_{A}$ $s_{b}=X_{b}$, because the rows of X sum
to zero; the rows of the matrix s also sum to zero, and $|s_{eb}|\le 2M/h_{A}$. Lift
each row through $B_{B}$. This gives a real matrix C with

$$
B_A C B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |C_{ef}|\le\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}.\tag{F.3}
$$

There is also an integral preimage $C_{0}$, without a claimed norm bound: express
X as a sum of $X_{ab}(e_a-e_{a_0})(e_b-e_{b_0})^{\mathsf T}$, for fixed roots $a_0,b_0$, and lift the
two differences along paths in A and B.

We round C while preserving its two-sided image. Choose a spanning tree of A.
Let P send an edge vector to the unique vector supported on that tree with the
same incidence. Thus $B_AP=B_A$ and P vanishes on $\ker B_A$. Put

$$
D=C-C_0,\qquad V=PD,\qquad U=D-V.
$$

Then $B_AU=0$. Also $B_A D B_B^{\mathsf T}=0$, so $P(DB_B^{\mathsf T})=0$ and hence $VB_B^{\mathsf T}=0$.
Round every column of U as a zero-divergence flow on A, and every row of V as
a zero-divergence flow on B. The resulting integral $U_{Z},V_{Z}$ retain those
identities and change each entry by less than one. Therefore
$Z=C_{0}+U_{Z}+V_{Z}$ proves (F.2). No bound on P is used. In particular this argument
does not assume that a tensor product of incidence matrices is totally
unimodular.

### F.2. A bounded-degree expander at every size

For each $n\ge 1$ there is a simple graph G on n vertices with maximum degree at
most eight and expansion $h=1/20$. The one-vertex case is immediate. For larger
n, take four independent uniform permutations and form the undirected union
of their permutation edges, discarding loops and repetitions.

Here is the counting argument, including its numerical estimate. Fix a set S
of size $1\le s\le n/2$ and put $r=\lfloor (s-1)/20\rfloor$. A permutation with at most r images
leaving S maps S into $S\cup R$ for some r-set R outside S. Its probability is
at most

$$
\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns.
$$

Consequently the probability that some s-set is bad for all four permutations
is at most

$$
U_s=\binom ns\left[\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns\right]^4.
$$

We verify $U_{s}\le 2^{-s}$. Write $A=\binom{n}{r}$, $B=\binom{s+r}{s}$,
$\alpha=s/n$ and $x=(s+r)/n$. Since $B\le A$ and
$B/\binom{n}{s}\le x^{s}$ (compare factors of the two binomial coefficients),

$$
U_s\le A^5x^{3s}.
$$

The elementary estimate $\binom{n}{r}\le (3n/r)^{r}$ for $r\ge 1$ gives
$A^{20}\le (60/\alpha)^{s}$ when $20r\le s$. One way to see the latter implication is to
use the monotonicity of $(60n/t)^{t}$ for $0<t\le n$, at $t=20r$ and $t=s$.
The case $r=0$ gives the same inequality directly. Further,

$$
x^{20}\le(21/20)^{20}\alpha^{20}\le3\alpha^{20}.
$$

Raising the bound for $U_{s}$ to the twentieth power gives

$$
U_s^{20}\le[60^5\cdot27\cdot\alpha^{55}]^s\le(2^{-20})^s,
$$

because $\alpha\le 1/2$ and $60^{5}\cdot 27\le 2^{35}$. Summing $2^{-s}$ over the finite range
$1\le s\le \lfloor n/2\rfloor$ gives a number strictly less than one. Thus one tuple of
permutations works for every such set. For each S, some permutation has at
least $r+1\ge s/20$ outgoing images. These give distinct edges of the simple
boundary, even after repetitions between permutations are discarded. Taking
complements proves (F.1) for every set. Each permutation contributes at most two
incident edges per vertex, giving degree at most eight. The cut inequality
also implies connectedness.

### F.3. A bounded signed filling in the complete cyclic host

Let Q have three classes A,B,C, each indexed by $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$, and all cyclic arcs
between consecutive classes. Fix an orientation of the graph G from Section F.2
on the index set. For indices a,b,c, write

$$
t(a,b,c)=[A_aB_b]+[B_bC_c]+[C_cA_a].
$$

Use the following fixed signed circulations as faces:

1. the $n^{2}$ Latin triangles t(a,b,a+b);
2. for every oriented edge $f\to s$ of G and every a, the two moves

$$
\begin{aligned}m_B(e,a)&=t(a,s,a+f)-t(a,f,a+f),\\m_C(e,a)&=t(a,f-a,s)-t(a,f-a,f);\end{aligned}
$$

3. in each of the three consecutive-class blocks, the rectangles
   $(e_s-e_f)(e_{s\prime}-e_{f\prime})^{\mathsf T}$ indexed by two oriented edges of G.

Each face is nonzero, has coefficients in {-1,0,1}, and has at most four
nonzero arcs. The moves have four, rather than six, arcs because a common
triangle side cancels. The only outgoing-profile change of $m_{B}$ is $e_{s}-e_{f}$
in class B; that of $m_{C}$ is $e_{s}-e_{f}$ in class C. Each rectangle has zero row
and column sums and therefore zero outgoing profile in every class.

There are at most $57n^{2}$ faces: G has at most $4n$ edges, so the three counts
are $n^{2}$, at most $8n^{2}$, and at most $48n^{2}$. For a fixed arc, bounds for the
numbers of incident faces in the four groups (triangles, B-moves, C-moves,
rectangles) are respectively

$$
3,\quad32,\quad32,\quad256.\tag{F.4}
$$

For the moves, choosing which of their two varying endpoints equals a fixed
index reduces the count to incident edges of G, with at most four such choices;
once this edge is fixed the remaining index is determined. For rectangles,
choose one endpoint of each oriented edge, giving the safe bound
$(2\cdot 8)^{2}$. The bound three for the Latin faces is deliberately loose. These
counts remain valid if different indexed faces have the same arc vector.

Let L be any balanced subgraph of Q. Denote its outgoing degrees in the three
classes by $d_{A},d_{B},d_{C}$. Their sums agree and every degree is at most n. Choose

$$
z_{ab}=\begin{cases}1,&\text{if the representative of }b-a\pmod n\text{ is }<d_A(a),\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

The chain sum $z_{ab}$ t(a,b,a+b) has the required A-profile. Its B- and C-profile
errors have sum zero and absolute value at most n. By Section F.1 each error has
an integral flow on G with coefficients of absolute value less than $20n+1$.
Split each coefficient into n integral summands of absolute value at most 21.
Use these summands as coefficients of $m_{B}(e,a)$, respectively $m_{C}(e,a)$.
The two corrections affect only their respective profiles. We obtain a signed
circulation Y with exactly the outgoing profile of L in all three classes.

By (F.4), the absolute face usage on any arc in this construction is at most

$$
3+2\cdot21\cdot32=1347.
$$

The residual $X=1_{L}-Y$ consequently has entries bounded by 1348. All its
outgoing profiles vanish. As it is a circulation, its incoming profiles also
vanish. Each consecutive-class matrix therefore has zero rows and columns.
Apply (F.2) with both expansion constants 1/20 to each of these three matrices.
The rectangle coefficients are integers with absolute value less than

$$
2\cdot1348\cdot20^2+2=1078402,
$$

hence at most 1078401. Combining this with (F.4) gives a signed filling of $1_{L}$
whose total absolute usage on every arc is at most the fixed integer

$$
T=3+2\cdot21\cdot32+1078401\cdot256.\tag{F.5}
$$

The faces and T were fixed before L. The filling coefficients depend on L.

### F.4. Converting signed fillings to a positive catalogue

Fix D subset Q. For each arc $e=u\to v$ of Q, introduce T internally private
positive paths from u to v of length four and T internally private negative
paths from v to u of length five. Distinct paths have distinct internal
vertices and distinct arcs. Their lengths have the appropriate residues
modulo three, so all paths are cyclic. Let R be their union, disjoint from D.

The catalogue consists of three types of positive balanced pieces:

- for every face, either sign, and every choice of a channel on each of its
  nonzero arcs, replace each signed arc by a path in its indicated direction;
- for every arc of Q, the union of any positive and any negative channel;
- for every e in D, e together with the zeroth negative channel for e.

Replacing an integral circulation by directed paths preserves balance.
Every listed piece is nonempty and contains at most 20 arcs. In particular,
the first type is not asserted to be a single directed cycle; balance is the
property used by the subsequent construction.

We prove exact coverage, not just coverage of L. Given balanced L subset D,
take the filling from Section F.3 and expand its coefficients into signed unit
occurrences. At an arc e, let $p_{e},n_{e}$ be their positive and negative counts.
Then

$$
p_e-n_e=\mathbf1_L(e),\qquad p_e+n_e\le T.
$$

For e in L first select the third-type piece using negative channel zero.
Assign distinct positive channels to the $p_{e}$ positive occurrences and distinct
remaining negative channels to the $n_{e}$ negative occurrences. There is enough
space, since $n_{e}+1_{L}(e)=p_{e}\le T$. The unassigned positive and negative channels
both number $T-p_{e}$, so pair them and select the second-type pieces. The
first-type pieces realize the signed face occurrences. Every arc of $R\cup L$
is now used exactly once. Pieces selected this way are distinct, since they
are nonempty and arc-disjoint. Thus they form a subset of the fixed catalogue,
not a multiset requiring extra copies of a physical arc.

The catalogue has size at most $C_{\rm card}n^2$ and vertex load at most $C_{\rm load}n$,
where the frozen constants are

$$
\begin{aligned}C_{\rm card}&=114T^4+9T^2+9,\\C_{\rm load}&=(646T^4+T^2+1)(120T+22),\\C_d&=C_{\rm card}+C_{\rm load}.\end{aligned}\tag{F.6}
$$

For the first estimate there are at most $2\cdot 57n^{2}\cdot T^{4}$ face pieces,
$9n^{2}\cdot T^{2}$ paired-channel pieces, and $9n^{2}$ input pieces. The bounds $9n^{2}$ count
all ordered pairs, so they safely overestimate the arcs of Q.

For the load estimate, a physical arc belongs to at most
$2\cdot 323\cdot T^{4}+T^{2}+1$ catalogue pieces. A base vertex touches at most $6n$ reference
arcs. Counting at most five arcs per channel and allowing one additional
channel token for a private vertex gives at most

$$
2[5(2T\cdot6n+1)+6n]\le(120T+22)n.
$$

incident physical arcs, for $n\ge 1$. Double counting pairs (piece, incident arc)
proves (F.6). These deliberately loose bounds cover both base and private
vertices. An arbitrary cyclic digraph D on N vertices embeds in Q with N
indices per class; padding preserves its original vertices. Formula (F.6) gives
a fixed reserve and catalogue with count $\le C_dN^2$ and load $\le C_dN$.
For $N=0$ use the empty reserve and catalogue. This proves the dense producer
with piece size twenty; it is not an additional hypothesis.

### F.5. Reducing a degree-seventeen input to square-root load

Let Y be cyclic with $d_{Y}(v)\le 17$ and $m=|Y|>0$. Put

$$
s=\lfloor\sqrt{2m}\rfloor+1,\quad M=307+290s,\quad A_0=9\cdot597^2\cdot8.\tag{F.7}
$$

We assign the support of Y to M groups in each colour, each with at most s
vertices, so that distinct arcs of Y have distinct ordered pairs of groups.
Process vertices one at a time. In addition to group capacity, maintain that
vertices at undirected distance at most two receive different group indices.
At a new vertex the forbidden group indices are bounded by:

- $17+17^{2}=306$ from vertices at distance at most two;
- $17^2s=289s$ from existing arcs whose group pair would coincide with an arc
  to a previously processed neighbour;
- at most s-1 full groups, since the processed support has size less than $s^{2}$.

For the second count, a group contains at most s old vertices, each meeting at
most seventeen arcs; there are at most seventeen relevant neighbours. Distinct
new arcs cannot collide with each other, because their old endpoints have
different group indices. Opposite orientations at the new vertex cannot
collide: their endpoint colours differ. Since M is larger than the sum of the
three exclusions, a group is always available. This establishes the claimed
assignment, rather than merely assuming a simple quotient.

Let p(v) be the group of v and let D be the cyclic quotient, with one hub per
group. The map e->(p(tail e),p(head e)) is injective. There are $N=3M$ hubs and
at most $17s$ input arcs incident with any one hub. Since $s^{2}\le 8m$ and $M\le 597s$,

$$
N^2\le A_0m,\qquad(\text{hub incidence})^2\le A_0m.\tag{F.8}
$$

Use Section F.4 on D. For each original arc $e=u\to v$ introduce five private
vertices and the following paths:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_e&:v\to x_0\to u,\\O_e&:u\to x_1\to x_2\to p(u),\\I_e&:p(v)\to x_3\to x_4\to v,\\Q_e&:p(u)\to p(v).\end{aligned}
$$

The colours of p(u),p(v) equal those of u,v. Thus the indicated paths are
cyclic. The base cycle $P_{e}+O_{e}+Q_{e}+I_{e}$ has length nine. The reserve consists
of all these base cycles and the dense reserve on the hubs. Its catalogue
contains the dense catalogue and:

- the triangle $e+P_{e}$, for each e in Y;
- the base cycle of length nine for each e;
- $I_{e}+O_{f}$, a cycle of length six, whenever $head(e)=tail(f)$.

Given balanced L subset Y, select the base cycle for each e outside L and the
triangle for each e in L. At each old vertex pair its incoming L-arcs with
its outgoing L-arcs, and use the corresponding six-cycles. The remaining
arcs are exactly the dense reserve plus Q(L). The latter is balanced, because
the group map preserves sums of divergences, and is a subgraph of D by
injectivity. Section F.4 partitions this remainder. All selections are
arc-disjoint; all pieces belong to the catalogue fixed before L.

There are at most $17m$ compatible ordered pairs (e,f), so the total catalogue
size is at most (19+C_d A_0)m. The following load calculation records the
stronger bound needed later for vertices which will be identified.
At a vertex w let $S_{w}$ be the sum of its degrees in all base nine-cycles.
The triangles contribute at most $S_{w}+d_{Y}(w)$, the base cycles at most $S_{w}$,
and the six-cycles at most $34S_{w}$: an arc can be the first or second member
of at most seventeen pairs. The dense catalogue contributes at most $C_{d}$ N
and does not meet any old vertex. In particular $S_{v}=2d_{Y}(v)$ at an old vertex,
and hence

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73d_Y(v)\quad\text{for every old vertex}.\tag{F.9}
$$

At a general vertex, let ell be its hub incidence if it is a hub, and zero
otherwise. The number of base cycles meeting it is at most 17+ell, giving

$$
\operatorname{load}(w)\le1241+(72+C_d)(\ell+N).
$$

By (F.8), $(\ell+N)^2\le(2A_0)^2m$. Since $m\ge 1$, the frozen constant

$$
C_m=19+C_dA_0+1241+(72+C_d)(2A_0).\tag{F.10}
$$

therefore bounds catalogue size by $C_{m}$ m and gives
$\operatorname{load}(w)^2\le C_m^2m$ at every vertex. Every piece has size at most twenty.
For $m=0$ the empty catalogue satisfies the same assertions. The distinction
between (F.9) and the square-root bound is essential: a square-root bound per
port would be inadequate after many ports are assigned to one physical root.

### F.6. A fixed eight-permutation network at each root

For every finite set P there are eight permutations such that, for every
S subset P, the total number of directed permutation channels leaving S,
counted with their permutation labels, is at least

$$
\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.\tag{F.11}
$$

Here parallel channels are retained as different channels; this is not the
simple graph used in Section F.2. For $|P|\le 1$ the assertion is immediate. Let
$n=|P|$ and fix S with $1\le s\le n/2$, $p=s/n$. For a uniform permutation let I be the
number of images from S which stay in S. Its factorial moments satisfy

$$
\mathbb E\binom Ik=\frac{\binom sk^2}{\binom nk}\le\binom skp^k.
$$

Thus E $\lambda^{I}$ $\le (1+p(\lambda-1))^{s}$ for $\lambda\ge 1$. If eight independent
permutations have fewer than s outgoing channels, their total internal count
exceeds $7s$. Markov's inequality with $\lambda=4/p$, followed by
$\binom{n}{s}\le (3/p)^{s}$, bounds the probability of a bad s-set by

$$
\left[3(5-p)^8p^6/4^7\right]^s\le2^{-s}.
$$

For the last inequality, $p^{3}(5-p)^{4}$ is increasing for $0<p\le 1/2$ and is less
than 52 there, while $3\cdot 52^{2}<4^{7}/2$. The sum over s is strictly less than one.
Some tuple therefore works for all small sets. The outgoing count across a
cut equals that across its complement for each permutation, proving (F.11).

Discard fixed points and regard each remaining channel as having unit
capacity. The in-degree and out-degree are each at most eight. If integers
$b_{p}$ satisfy $|b_{p}|\le 1$ and sum $b_{p}=0$, then

$$
\left|\sum_{p\in S}b_p\right|\le\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.
$$

By (F.11) all directed cut conditions for routing this imbalance hold. An
integral unit-capacity flow therefore selects channels with the required
divergence. This last assertion also follows directly by adjoining a source
and sink for the positive and negative demands and augmenting along residual
paths: if augmentation stops before all demand is routed, the source-reachable
set violates precisely one of these cut inequalities. Integral capacities
keep every selected channel at value zero or one. The network works for all
such b; it is not chosen after b is known.

### F.7. Root ports and the completed catalogue

Let X be an arbitrary cyclic digraph and put $x=|X|$. Split each input arc into
two distinct ports, one assigned to its tail root and one to its head root.
The lifted input is a matching on $2x$ ports. A port retains the colour of its
root. For each root apply Section F.6 to its set of ports. Replace every selected
network channel by a private path of length three, whose endpoints are its
ports. The endpoints have the same colour, so this path is cyclic. Let N be
the union of all network paths and I the lifted input.

Every port has network total degree at most sixteen, every network internal
vertex has degree two, and the lifted matching adds at most one. Hence

$$
\max_v d_{N\cup I}(v)\le17,\qquad |N\cup I|\le49x.\tag{F.12}
$$

Indeed there are at most eight channels per port, each with three arcs, so
$|N|\le 24\cdot (2x)$. The networks are fixed for X. If L subset X is balanced, its
lift has divergence in {-1,0,1} at every port and the sum of divergences in
each root fibre is zero. Section F.6 selects whole channels whose paths A
cancel these divergences. Thus A union I(L) is balanced, with A subset N.

Apply Section F.5 once to $Y=N\cup I$, producing a reserve R disjoint from Y
and its fixed catalogue. Enlarge this catalogue by every individual channel
path of N. Given L, first use the mesoscopic partition for A union I(L).
Then add the individual channel paths not selected in A. This partitions

$$
R\cup N\cup I(L).\tag{F.13}
$$

exactly, using a subset of the enlarged fixed catalogue.

An individual added channel path is not balanced on the split port set. Its
two endpoints belong to the same root. After identification with that root,
its incoming and outgoing contributions cancel. All other pieces were already
balanced. The physical embedding must preserve distinct arcs; that separate
step in Section 8 of this article is not replaced by an arbitrary quotient
of the abstract graph. Under an arc-injective realization, balance descends
by summing divergences over fibres, and the partitions in (F.13) descend too.

There are at most $16x$ extra channel pieces. Their load at an old vertex is
at most its network degree, since the paths have disjoint arcs. Equations
(F.9) and (F.12) therefore give the uniform old-vertex bound

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73\cdot17+16=1257.\tag{F.14}
$$

For a genuinely new mesoscopic vertex u there are no extra channel pieces,
so $load(u)^{2}\le C_{m}^{2}\cdot 49x$. The remaining bounds are

$$
\begin{aligned}|\mathcal C|&\le(49C_m+16)x,\\\sum_{P\in\mathcal C}|P|&\le(980C_m+48)x.\end{aligned}\tag{F.15}
$$

and every piece has at most twenty arcs. The second bound keeps the sizes
twenty and three separate; replacing both by twenty is unnecessary.

There are exactly $d_{X}(r)$ ports assigned to a physical root r. The total
catalogue precharge carried by those ports is therefore at most

$$
1257d_X(r).\tag{F.16}
$$

not 1257 times the total number of input arcs. Network internal vertices are
not pinned to r. This is the root budget used by the weighted physical
embedding. Taking L empty in (F.13) also proves that the support of the catalogue
contains R union N, which is needed when its arc weights are defined.

Equations (F.12)--(F.16) complete the abstract catalogue construction. Together
with an arc-injective physical realization and the terminal absorber proved
in Appendix A, they supply the missing abstract input
to the conserved-family construction. This statement concerns that input; the separate PAR/BAL and semidense proofs are given in Appendices E and C, respectively.

### F.8. Why the pieces meet the terminal divisibility conditions

For the three-colour core the only triangle type is 012. At a vertex of colour
i in a balanced cyclic piece P, the numbers of neighbours of colours i-1 and
i+1 agree: they are its incoming and outgoing degrees. Its local profile is
therefore an integral multiple of the corner profile of 012. Summing balance
over each colour class also shows that the numbers of arcs in the three
consecutive-class blocks agree. The global edge-count vector is consequently
an integral multiple of (1,1,1). Thus P satisfies both integer divisibility
conditions; total edge-count divisibility alone is not the argument.

After the physical replacement in this article, the same reasoning applies
because every piece is balanced and cyclic, including the extra channels
whose ends were identified with their common root. Each piece has at most
eighty physical edges. The bounded integer-certificate result in Appendix A may therefore be used with the single size bound eighty. Its
certificate is constructed in the complete allowed host; one must not assert
that all of its auxiliary triangles already lie in the incomplete host.
Instead the terminal gadget is embedded using extension. Its graph has no
edge between two old roots, and its construction orders the new vertices
with at most four previously exposed neighbours, as proved in Appendix A.
The supply and avoidance inequalities there are the conditions used for this
embedding.

Finally, apply the fixed-catalogue assembly lemma to the physical catalogue.
Its count and whole-catalogue load, rather than the load of any particular
residual selection, are the inputs to that lemma. The terminal gadgets and
their physical embeddings are fixed for all pieces before L is selected.
The partition for L then chooses one of the two decompositions of each
already embedded gadget. This explains precisely where (F.15), (F.16) and the
physical load estimate enter; it does not introduce a new absorber depending
on L. The quantitative choice of the host scales remains the one in the
frozen producer and the physical realization lemma of Section 8.

particular residual graph. All reserves and catalogues below are chosen before
the residual $L$. Only the partition selected from the catalogue depends on $L$.

### F.1. Integer rounding and a two-sided inverse

Orient the edges of a finite simple graph arbitrarily and let $B$ be its signed
incidence matrix, with a column $e_{v}-e_{u}$ for an edge oriented from $u$ to $v$.

**Flow rounding.** If $Bf$ is integral, there is an integral vector $z$ with $Bz=Bf$
and $\lfloor f_e\rfloor\le z_e\le\lceil f_e\rceil$ for every edge $e$. In particular $|z_{e}-f_{e}|<1$.

To see this, consider the edges on which $f$ is not integral. No vertex has exactly
one such incident edge: its incidence equation would have a nonintegral left
side and an integral right side. If any such edge remains, their underlying
graph therefore contains a cycle. Add a signed multiple of its cyclic incidence
vector. This preserves $Bf$. Increase the multiple until an edge first reaches an
integer endpoint of its allowed interval. No other coordinate leaves its
interval, and at least one nonintegral coordinate disappears. Previously
integral coordinates are not changed. Iteration terminates, proving the claim.

Suppose $G$ satisfies the cut inequality

$$
|\partial_G S|\ge h\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\},\qquad h>0.\tag{F.1}
$$

Every zero-sum real vector $g$ with $|g_{v}|\le M$ has a real preimage under $B$ of
supremum norm at most $M/h$. Indeed,

$$
\left|\sum_{v\in S}g_v\right|\le M\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\}\le(M/h)|\partial_G S|.
$$

These cut inequalities imply the flow assertion. For completeness, the image
of the box $[-M/h,M/h]^E$ under $B$ is a compact convex set. If $g$ were outside it,
a separating potential $p$ would satisfy

$$
\langle p,g\rangle>(M/h)\sum_{uv\in E}|p_u-p_v|.
$$

Subtract a constant from $p$, which does not change the left side, and express $p$
as a sum of indicators of its nested level sets multiplied by consecutive
level differences. Apply the cut inequality to each term and sum. This gives
the reverse inequality, a contradiction. Integral $g$ can then be rounded as
above without changing its divergence.

**Two-sided inverse.** Let A and $B$ be connected graphs with expansion constants
$h_{A},h_{B}$. If $X$ is an integral matrix with zero row and column sums and
$|X_{ab}|\le M$, then

$$
B_A Z B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |Z_{ef}|<\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}+2.\tag{F.2}
$$

for an integral matrix $Z$.

First lift each column of $X$ through $B_{A}$, obtaining columns $u_{b}$ bounded by
$M/h_{A}$. Set $s_b=u_b-\operatorname{mean}_{b\prime}u_{b\prime}$. Then $B_{A}$ $s_{b}=X_{b}$, because the rows of $X$ sum
to zero; the rows of the matrix $s$ also sum to zero, and $|s_{eb}|\le 2M/h_{A}$. Lift
each row through $B_{B}$. This gives a real matrix $C$ with

$$
B_A C B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |C_{ef}|\le\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}.\tag{F.3}
$$

There is also an integral preimage $C_{0}$, without a claimed norm bound: express
$X$ as a sum of $X_{ab}(e_a-e_{a_0})(e_b-e_{b_0})^{\mathsf T}$, for fixed roots $a_0,b_0$, and lift the
two differences along paths in $A$ and $B$.

We round $C$ while preserving its two-sided image. Choose a spanning tree of $A$.
Let $P$ send an edge vector to the unique vector supported on that tree with the
same incidence. Thus $B_AP=B_A$ and $P$ vanishes on $\ker B_A$. Put

$$
D=C-C_0,\qquad V=PD,\qquad U=D-V.
$$

Then $B_AU=0$. Also $B_A D B_B^{\mathsf T}=0$, so $P(DB_B^{\mathsf T})=0$ and hence $VB_B^{\mathsf T}=0$.
Round every column of $U$ as a zero-divergence flow on $A$, and every row of $V$ as
a zero-divergence flow on $B$. The resulting integral $U_{Z},V_{Z}$ retain those
identities and change each entry by less than one. Therefore
$Z=C_{0}+U_{Z}+V_{Z}$ proves (F.2). No bound on $P$ is used. In particular this argument
does not assume that a tensor product of incidence matrices is totally
unimodular.

### F.2. A bounded-degree expander at every size

For each $n\ge 1$ there is a simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree at
most eight and expansion $h=1/20$. The one-vertex case is immediate. For larger
$n$, take four independent uniform permutations and form the undirected union
of their permutation edges, discarding loops and repetitions.

Here is the counting argument, including its numerical estimate. Fix a set $S$
of size $1\le s\le n/2$ and put $r=\lfloor (s-1)/20\rfloor$. A permutation with at most $r$ images
leaving $S$ maps $S$ into $S\cup R$ for some $r$-set $R$ outside $S$. Its probability is
at most

$$
\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns.
$$

Consequently the probability that some $s$-set is bad for all four permutations
is at most

$$
U_s=\binom ns\left[\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns\right]^4.
$$

We verify $U_{s}\le 2^{-s}$. Write $A=\binom{n}{r}$, $B=\binom{s+r}{s}$,
$\alpha=s/n$ and $x=(s+r)/n$. Since $B\le A$ and
$B/\binom{n}{s}\le x^{s}$ (compare factors of the two binomial coefficients),

$$
U_s\le A^5x^{3s}.
$$

The elementary estimate $\binom{n}{r}\le (3n/r)^{r}$ for $r\ge 1$ gives
$A^{20}\le (60/\alpha)^{s}$ when $20r\le s$. One way to see the latter implication is to
use the monotonicity of $(60n/t)^{t}$ for $0<t\le n$, at $t=20r$ and $t=s$.
The case $r=0$ gives the same inequality directly. Further,

$$
x^{20}\le(21/20)^{20}\alpha^{20}\le3\alpha^{20}.
$$

Raising the bound for $U_{s}$ to the twentieth power gives

$$
U_s^{20}\le[60^5\cdot27\cdot\alpha^{55}]^s\le(2^{-20})^s,
$$

because $\alpha\le 1/2$ and $60^{5}\cdot 27\le 2^{35}$. Summing $2^{-s}$ over the finite range
$1\le s\le \lfloor n/2\rfloor$ gives a number strictly less than one. Thus one tuple of
permutations works for every such set. For each $S$, some permutation has at
least $r+1\ge s/20$ outgoing images. These give distinct edges of the simple
boundary, even after repetitions between permutations are discarded. Taking
complements proves (F.1) for every set. Each permutation contributes at most two
incident edges per vertex, giving degree at most eight. The cut inequality
also implies connectedness.

### F.3. A bounded signed filling in the complete cyclic host

Let $Q$ have three classes $A,B,C$, each indexed by $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$, and all cyclic arcs
between consecutive classes. Fix an orientation of the graph $G$ from Section F.2
on the index set. For indices $a,b,c$, write

$$
t(a,b,c)=[A_aB_b]+[B_bC_c]+[C_cA_a].
$$

Use the following fixed signed circulations as faces:

1. the $n^{2}$ Latin triangles $t(a,b,a+b)$;
2. for every oriented edge $f\to s$ of $G$ and every $a$, the two moves

$$
\begin{aligned}m_B(e,a)&=t(a,s,a+f)-t(a,f,a+f),\\m_C(e,a)&=t(a,f-a,s)-t(a,f-a,f);\end{aligned}
$$

3. in each of the three consecutive-class blocks, the rectangles
   $(e_s-e_f)(e_{s\prime}-e_{f\prime})^{\mathsf T}$ indexed by two oriented edges of $G$.

Each face is nonzero, has coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$, and has at most four
nonzero arcs. The moves have four, rather than six, arcs because a common
triangle side cancels. The only outgoing-profile change of $m_{B}$ is $e_{s}-e_{f}$
in class $B$; that of $m_{C}$ is $e_{s}-e_{f}$ in class $C$. Each rectangle has zero row
and column sums and therefore zero outgoing profile in every class.

There are at most $57n^{2}$ faces: $G$ has at most $4n$ edges, so the three counts
are $n^{2}$, at most $8n^{2}$, and at most $48n^{2}$. For a fixed arc, bounds for the
numbers of incident faces in the four groups (triangles, $B$-moves, $C$-moves,
rectangles) are respectively

$$
3,\quad32,\quad32,\quad256.\tag{F.4}
$$

For the moves, choosing which of their two varying endpoints equals a fixed
index reduces the count to incident edges of $G$, with at most four such choices;
once this edge is fixed the remaining index is determined. For rectangles,
choose one endpoint of each oriented edge, giving the safe bound
$(2\cdot 8)^{2}$. The bound three for the Latin faces is deliberately loose. These
counts remain valid if different indexed faces have the same arc vector.

Let $L$ be any balanced subgraph of $Q$. Denote its outgoing degrees in the three
classes by $d_{A},d_{B},d_{C}$. Their sums agree and every degree is at most $n$. Choose

$$
z_{ab}=\begin{cases}1,&\text{if the representative of }b-a\pmod n\text{ is }<d_A(a),\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

The chain sum $z_{ab}$ $t(a,b,a+b)$ has the required A-profile. Its $B$- and $C$-profile
errors have sum zero and absolute value at most $n$. By Section F.1 each error has
an integral flow on $G$ with coefficients of absolute value less than $20n+1$.
Split each coefficient into $n$ integral summands of absolute value at most 21.
Use these summands as coefficients of $m_{B}(e,a)$, respectively $m_{C}(e,a)$.
The two corrections affect only their respective profiles. We obtain a signed
circulation $Y$ with exactly the outgoing profile of $L$ in all three classes.

By (F.4), the absolute face usage on any arc in this construction is at most

$$
3+2\cdot21\cdot32=1347.
$$

The residual $X=1_{L}-Y$ consequently has entries bounded by 1348. All its
outgoing profiles vanish. As it is a circulation, its incoming profiles also
vanish. Each consecutive-class matrix therefore has zero rows and columns.
Apply (F.2) with both expansion constants 1/20 to each of these three matrices.
The rectangle coefficients are integers with absolute value less than

$$
2\cdot1348\cdot20^2+2=1078402,
$$

hence at most 1078401. Combining this with (F.4) gives a signed filling of $1_{L}$
whose total absolute usage on every arc is at most the fixed integer

$$
T=3+2\cdot21\cdot32+1078401\cdot256.\tag{F.5}
$$

The faces and $T$ were fixed before $L$. The filling coefficients depend on $L$.

### F.4. Converting signed fillings to a positive catalogue

Fix $D\subseteq Q$. For each arc $e=u\to v$ of $Q$, introduce $T$ internally private
positive paths from $u$ to $v$ of length four and $T$ internally private negative
paths from $v$ to $u$ of length five. Distinct paths have distinct internal
vertices and distinct arcs. Their lengths have the appropriate residues
modulo three, so all paths are cyclic. Let $R$ be their union, disjoint from $D$.

The catalogue consists of three types of positive balanced pieces:

- for every face, either sign, and every choice of a channel on each of its
  nonzero arcs, replace each signed arc by a path in its indicated direction;
- for every arc of $Q$, the union of any positive and any negative channel;
- for every $e\in D$, e together with the zeroth negative channel for e.

Replacing an integral circulation by directed paths preserves balance.
Every listed piece is nonempty and contains at most 20 arcs. In particular,
the first type is not asserted to be a single directed cycle; balance is the
property used by the subsequent construction.

We prove exact coverage, not just coverage of $L$. Given balanced $L\subseteq D$,
take the filling from Section F.3 and expand its coefficients into signed unit
occurrences. At an arc $e$, let $p_{e},n_{e}$ be their positive and negative counts.
Then

$$
p_e-n_e=\mathbf1_L(e),\qquad p_e+n_e\le T.
$$

For $e\in L$ first select the third-type piece using negative channel zero.
Assign distinct positive channels to the $p_{e}$ positive occurrences and distinct
remaining negative channels to the $n_{e}$ negative occurrences. There is enough
space, since $n_{e}+1_{L}(e)=p_{e}\le T$. The unassigned positive and negative channels
both number $T-p_{e}$, so pair them and select the second-type pieces. The
first-type pieces realize the signed face occurrences. Every arc of $R\cup L$
is now used exactly once. Pieces selected this way are distinct, since they
are nonempty and arc-disjoint. Thus they form a subset of the fixed catalogue,
not a multiset requiring extra copies of a physical arc.

The catalogue has size at most $C_{\rm card}n^2$ and vertex load at most $C_{\rm load}n$,
where the frozen constants are

$$
\begin{aligned}C_{\rm card}&=114T^4+9T^2+9,\\C_{\rm load}&=(646T^4+T^2+1)(120T+22),\\C_d&=C_{\rm card}+C_{\rm load}.\end{aligned}\tag{F.6}
$$

For the first estimate there are at most $2\cdot 57n^{2}\cdot T^{4}$ face pieces,
$9n^{2}\cdot T^{2}$ paired-channel pieces, and $9n^{2}$ input pieces. The bounds $9n^{2}$ count
all ordered pairs, so they safely overestimate the arcs of $Q$.

For the load estimate, a physical arc belongs to at most
$2\cdot 323\cdot T^{4}+T^{2}+1$ catalogue pieces. A base vertex touches at most $6n$ reference
arcs. Counting at most five arcs per channel and allowing one additional
channel token for a private vertex gives at most

$$
2[5(2T\cdot6n+1)+6n]\le(120T+22)n.
$$

incident physical arcs, for $n\ge 1$. Double counting pairs (piece, incident arc)
proves (F.6). These deliberately loose bounds cover both base and private
vertices. An arbitrary cyclic digraph $D$ on $N$ vertices embeds in $Q$ with $N$
indices per class; padding preserves its original vertices. Formula (F.6) gives
a fixed reserve and catalogue with count $\le C_dN^2$ and load $\le C_dN$.
For $N=0$ use the empty reserve and catalogue. This proves the dense producer
with piece size twenty; it is not an additional hypothesis.

### F.5. Reducing a degree-seventeen input to square-root load

Let $Y$ be cyclic with $d_{Y}(v)\le 17$ and $m=|Y|>0$. Put

$$
s=\lfloor\sqrt{2m}\rfloor+1,\quad M=307+290s,\quad A_0=9\cdot597^2\cdot8.\tag{F.7}
$$

We assign the support of $Y$ to $M$ groups in each colour, each with at most $s$
vertices, so that distinct arcs of $Y$ have distinct ordered pairs of groups.
Process vertices one at a time. In addition to group capacity, maintain that
vertices at undirected distance at most two receive different group indices.
At a new vertex the forbidden group indices are bounded by:

- $17+17^{2}=306$ from vertices at distance at most two;
- $17^2s=289s$ from existing arcs whose group pair would coincide with an arc
  to a previously processed neighbour;
- at most $s-1$ full groups, since the processed support has size less than $s^{2}$.

For the second count, a group contains at most $s$ old vertices, each meeting at
most seventeen arcs; there are at most seventeen relevant neighbours. Distinct
new arcs cannot collide with each other, because their old endpoints have
different group indices. Opposite orientations at the new vertex cannot
collide: their endpoint colours differ. Since $M$ is larger than the sum of the
three exclusions, a group is always available. This establishes the claimed
assignment, rather than merely assuming a simple quotient.

Let $p(v)$ be the group of $v$ and let $D$ be the cyclic quotient, with one hub per
group. The map $e\mapsto(p(\operatorname{tail}e),p(\operatorname{head}e))$ is injective. There are $N=3M$ hubs and
at most $17s$ input arcs incident with any one hub. Since $s^{2}\le 8m$ and $M\le 597s$,

$$
N^2\le A_0m,\qquad(\text{hub incidence})^2\le A_0m.\tag{F.8}
$$

Use Section F.4 on $D$. For each original arc $e=u\to v$ introduce five private
vertices and the following paths:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_e&:v\to x_0\to u,\\O_e&:u\to x_1\to x_2\to p(u),\\I_e&:p(v)\to x_3\to x_4\to v,\\Q_e&:p(u)\to p(v).\end{aligned}
$$

The colours of $p(u),p(v)$ equal those of $u,v$. Thus the indicated paths are
cyclic. The base cycle $P_{e}+O_{e}+Q_{e}+I_{e}$ has length nine. The reserve consists
of all these base cycles and the dense reserve on the hubs. Its catalogue
contains the dense catalogue and:

- the triangle $e+P_{e}$, for each $e\in Y$;
- the base cycle of length nine for each e;
- $I_{e}+O_{f}$, a cycle of length six, whenever $head(e)=tail(f)$.

Given balanced $L\subseteq Y$, select the base cycle for each e outside $L$ and the
triangle for each $e\in L$. At each old vertex pair its incoming $L$-arcs with
its outgoing $L$-arcs, and use the corresponding six-cycles. The remaining
arcs are exactly the dense reserve plus $Q(L)$. The latter is balanced, because
the group map preserves sums of divergences, and is a subgraph of $D$ by
injectivity. Section F.4 partitions this remainder. All selections are
arc-disjoint; all pieces belong to the catalogue fixed before $L$.

There are at most $17m$ compatible ordered pairs $(e,f)$, so the total catalogue
size is at most $(19+C_d A_0)m$. The following load calculation records the
stronger bound needed later for vertices which will be identified.
At a vertex $w$ let $S_{w}$ be the sum of its degrees in all base nine-cycles.
The triangles contribute at most $S_{w}+d_{Y}(w)$, the base cycles at most $S_{w}$,
and the six-cycles at most $34S_{w}$: an arc can be the first or second member
of at most seventeen pairs. The dense catalogue contributes at most $C_{d}$ $N$
and does not meet any old vertex. In particular $S_{v}=2d_{Y}(v)$ at an old vertex,
and hence

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73d_Y(v)\quad\text{for every old vertex}.\tag{F.9}
$$

At a general vertex, let $\ell$ be its hub incidence if it is a hub, and zero
otherwise. The number of base cycles meeting it is at most $17+\ell$, giving

$$
\operatorname{load}(w)\le1241+(72+C_d)(\ell+N).
$$

By (F.8), $(\ell+N)^2\le(2A_0)^2m$. Since $m\ge 1$, the frozen constant

$$
C_m=19+C_dA_0+1241+(72+C_d)(2A_0).\tag{F.10}
$$

therefore bounds catalogue size by $C_{m}$ $m$ and gives
$\operatorname{load}(w)^2\le C_m^2m$ at every vertex. Every piece has size at most twenty.
For $m=0$ the empty catalogue satisfies the same assertions. The distinction
between (F.9) and the square-root bound is essential: a square-root bound per
port would be inadequate after many ports are assigned to one physical root.

### F.6. A fixed eight-permutation network at each root

For every finite set $P$ there are eight permutations such that, for every
$S\subseteq P$, the total number of directed permutation channels leaving $S$,
counted with their permutation labels, is at least

$$
\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.\tag{F.11}
$$

Here parallel channels are retained as different channels; this is not the
simple graph used in Section F.2. For $|P|\le 1$ the assertion is immediate. Let
$n=|P|$ and fix $S$ with $1\le s\le n/2$, $p=s/n$. For a uniform permutation let $I$ be the
number of images from $S$ which stay in $S$. Its factorial moments satisfy

$$
\mathbb E\binom Ik=\frac{\binom sk^2}{\binom nk}\le\binom skp^k.
$$

Thus $\mathbb E$ $\lambda^{I}$ $\le (1+p(\lambda-1))^{s}$ for $\lambda\ge 1$. If eight independent
permutations have fewer than $s$ outgoing channels, their total internal count
exceeds $7s$. Markov'$s$ inequality with $\lambda=4/p$, followed by
$\binom{n}{s}\le (3/p)^{s}$, bounds the probability of a bad $s$-set by

$$
\left[3(5-p)^8p^6/4^7\right]^s\le2^{-s}.
$$

For the last inequality, $p^{3}(5-p)^{4}$ is increasing for $0<p\le 1/2$ and is less
than 52 there, while $3\cdot 52^{2}<4^{7}/2$. The sum over $s$ is strictly less than one.
Some tuple therefore works for all small sets. The outgoing count across a
cut equals that across its complement for each permutation, proving (F.11).

Discard fixed points and regard each remaining channel as having unit
capacity. The in-degree and out-degree are each at most eight. If integers
$b_{p}$ satisfy $|b_{p}|\le 1$ and sum $b_{p}=0$, then

$$
\left|\sum_{p\in S}b_p\right|\le\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.
$$

By (F.11) all directed cut conditions for routing this imbalance hold. An
integral unit-capacity flow therefore selects channels with the required
divergence. This last assertion also follows directly by adjoining a source
and sink for the positive and negative demands and augmenting along residual
paths: if augmentation stops before all demand is routed, the source-reachable
set violates precisely one of these cut inequalities. Integral capacities
keep every selected channel at value zero or one. The network works for all
such $b$; it is not chosen after $b$ is known.

### F.7. Root ports and the completed catalogue

Let $X$ be an arbitrary cyclic digraph and put $x=|X|$. Split each input arc into
two distinct ports, one assigned to its tail root and one to its head root.
The lifted input is a matching on $2x$ ports. A port retains the colour of its
root. For each root apply Section F.6 to its set of ports. Replace every selected
network channel by a private path of length three, whose endpoints are its
ports. The endpoints have the same colour, so this path is cyclic. Let $N$ be
the union of all network paths and $I$ the lifted input.

Every port has network total degree at most sixteen, every network internal
vertex has degree two, and the lifted matching adds at most one. Hence

$$
\max_v d_{N\cup I}(v)\le17,\qquad |N\cup I|\le49x.\tag{F.12}
$$

Indeed there are at most eight channels per port, each with three arcs, so
$|N|\le 24\cdot (2x)$. The networks are fixed for $X$. If $L\subseteq X$ is balanced, its
lift has divergence in $\{-1,0,1\}$ at every port and the sum of divergences in
each root fibre is zero. Section F.6 selects whole channels whose paths $A$
cancel these divergences. Thus $A\cup I(L)$ is balanced, with $A\subseteq N$.

Apply Section F.5 once to $Y=N\cup I$, producing a reserve $R$ disjoint from $Y$
and its fixed catalogue. Enlarge this catalogue by every individual channel
path of $N$. Given $L$, first use the mesoscopic partition for $A\cup I(L)$.
Then add the individual channel paths not selected in $A$. This partitions

$$
R\cup N\cup I(L).\tag{F.13}
$$

exactly, using a subset of the enlarged fixed catalogue.

An individual added channel path is not balanced on the split port set. Its
two endpoints belong to the same root. After identification with that root,
its incoming and outgoing contributions cancel. All other pieces were already
balanced. The physical embedding must preserve distinct arcs; that separate
step in Section 8 of this article is not replaced by an arbitrary quotient
of the abstract graph. Under an arc-injective realization, balance descends
by summing divergences over fibres, and the partitions in (F.13) descend too.

There are at most $16x$ extra channel pieces. Their load at an old vertex is
at most its network degree, since the paths have disjoint arcs. Equations
(F.9) and (F.12) therefore give the uniform old-vertex bound

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73\cdot17+16=1257.\tag{F.14}
$$

For a genuinely new mesoscopic vertex $u$ there are no extra channel pieces,
so $load(u)^{2}\le C_{m}^{2}\cdot 49x$. The remaining bounds are

$$
\begin{aligned}|\mathcal C|&\le(49C_m+16)x,\\\sum_{P\in\mathcal C}|P|&\le(980C_m+48)x.\end{aligned}\tag{F.15}
$$

and every piece has at most twenty arcs. The second bound keeps the sizes
twenty and three separate; replacing both by twenty is unnecessary.

There are exactly $d_{X}(r)$ ports assigned to a physical root $r$. The total
catalogue precharge carried by those ports is therefore at most

$$
1257d_X(r).\tag{F.16}
$$

not 1257 times the total number of input arcs. Network internal vertices are
not pinned to $r$. This is the root budget used by the weighted physical
embedding. Taking $L$ empty in (F.13) also proves that the support of the catalogue
contains $R\cup N$, which is needed when its arc weights are defined.

Equations (F.12)--(F.16) complete the abstract catalogue construction. Together
with an arc-injective physical realization and the terminal absorber proved
in Appendix A, they supply the missing abstract input
to the conserved-family construction. This statement concerns that input; the separate PAR/BAL and semidense proofs are given in Appendices E and C, respectively.

### F.8. Why the pieces meet the terminal divisibility conditions

For the three-colour core the only triangle type is 012. At a vertex of colour
$i$ in a balanced cyclic piece $P$, the numbers of neighbours of colours $i-1$ and
$i+1$ agree: they are its incoming and outgoing degrees. Its local profile is
therefore an integral multiple of the corner profile of 012. Summing balance
over each colour class also shows that the numbers of arcs in the three
consecutive-class blocks agree. The global edge-count vector is consequently
an integral multiple of $(1,1,1)$. Thus $P$ satisfies both integer divisibility
conditions; total edge-count divisibility alone is not the argument.

After the physical replacement in this article, the same reasoning applies
because every piece is balanced and cyclic, including the extra channels
whose ends were identified with their common root. Each piece has at most
eighty physical edges. The bounded integer-certificate result in Appendix A may therefore be used with the single size bound eighty. Its
certificate is constructed in the complete allowed host; one must not assert
that all of its auxiliary triangles already lie in the incomplete host.
Instead the terminal gadget is embedded using extension. Its graph has no
edge between two old roots, and its construction orders the new vertices
with at most four previously exposed neighbours, as proved in Appendix A.
The supply and avoidance inequalities there are the conditions used for this
embedding.

Finally, apply the fixed-catalogue assembly lemma to the physical catalogue.
Its count and whole-catalogue load, rather than the load of any particular
residual selection, are the inputs to that lemma. The terminal gadgets and
their physical embeddings are fixed for all pieces before $L$ is selected.
The partition for $L$ then chooses one of the two decompositions of each
already embedded gadget. This explains precisely where (F.15), (F.16) and the
physical load estimate enter; it does not introduce a new absorber depending
on $L$. The quantitative choice of the host scales remains the one in the
frozen producer and the physical realization lemma of Section 8.

## Apéndice F. Un catálogo fijo para las familias con leyes de conservación

En todo este apéndice, un digrafo cíclico tiene tres clases de vértices y cada arco va de la clase i a la clase i+1 módulo 3. Los digrafos no tienen arcos repetidos. El grado d(v) significa **grado de entrada más grado de salida**. Una circulación con signos es un vector entero sobre los arcos cuyas sumas entrante y saliente son iguales en cada vértice. Una pieza positiva es un conjunto no vacío de arcos equilibrado en ese mismo sentido. No tiene por qué ser un único ciclo. Su tamaño es su número de arcos.

Para un catálogo finito C de piezas, su carga en v es

$$
\operatorname{load}_{\mathcal C}(v)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal C}d_P(v).
$$

Esto cuenta el catálogo completo, no sólo las piezas seleccionadas para un grafo residual concreto. Todas las reservas y catálogos que siguen se eligen antes del residuo L. Sólo la partición elegida del catálogo depende de L.

### F.1. Redondeo entero y una inversa bilateral

Orientamos arbitrariamente las aristas de un grafo simple finito y denotamos por B su matriz de incidencia con signos, con una columna $e_{v}-e_{u}$ para una arista orientada de u a v.

**Redondeo de flujos.** Si Bf es entero, existe un vector entero z con $Bz=Bf$ y $\lfloor f_e\rfloor\le z_e\le\lceil f_e\rceil$ para cada arista e. En particular, $|z_{e}-f_{e}|<1$.

Para verlo, consideramos las aristas en las que f no es entero. Ningún vértice tiene exactamente una arista incidente de ese tipo: su ecuación de incidencia tendría un lado izquierdo no entero y un lado derecho entero. Si queda alguna de esas aristas, su grafo subyacente contiene, por tanto, un ciclo. Añadimos un múltiplo con signo de su vector de incidencia cíclica. Esto preserva Bf. Aumentamos el múltiplo hasta que una arista alcance por primera vez un extremo entero de su intervalo permitido. Ninguna otra coordenada sale de su intervalo y desaparece al menos una coordenada no entera. Las coordenadas anteriormente enteras no cambian. La iteración termina y demuestra la afirmación.

Supongamos que G satisface la desigualdad de corte

$$
|\partial_G S|\ge h\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\},\qquad h>0.\tag{F.1}
$$

Todo vector real g de suma cero con $|g_{v}|\le M$ tiene una preimagen real bajo B de norma supremo a lo sumo M/h. En efecto,

$$
\left|\sum_{v\in S}g_v\right|\le M\min\{|S|,|V(G)\setminus S|\}\le(M/h)|\partial_G S|.
$$

Estas desigualdades de corte implican la afirmación sobre flujos. Para completar la prueba, la imagen de la caja $[-M/h,M/h]^E$ bajo B es un conjunto convexo compacto. Si g estuviera fuera, un potencial separador p satisfaría

$$
\langle p,g\rangle>(M/h)\sum_{uv\in E}|p_u-p_v|.
$$

Restamos una constante a p, lo que no cambia el lado izquierdo, y expresamos p como suma de indicadores de sus conjuntos de nivel anidados multiplicados por diferencias consecutivas de nivel. Aplicamos la desigualdad de corte a cada término y sumamos. Obtenemos la desigualdad opuesta, una contradicción. Si g es entero, podemos redondear como antes sin cambiar su divergencia.

**Inversa bilateral.** Sean A y B grafos conexos con constantes de expansión $h_{A},h_{B}$. Si X es una matriz entera con sumas de filas y columnas nulas y $|X_{ab}|\le M$, entonces

$$
B_A Z B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |Z_{ef}|<\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}+2.\tag{F.2}
$$

para una matriz entera Z.

Levantamos primero cada columna de X a través de $B_{A}$, obteniendo columnas $u_{b}$ acotadas por $M/h_{A}$. Pongamos $s_b=u_b-\operatorname{mean}_{b\prime}u_{b\prime}$. Entonces $B_{A}$ $s_{b}=X_{b}$, pues las filas de X suman cero; las filas de la matriz s también suman cero y $|s_{eb}|\le 2M/h_{A}$. Levantamos cada fila a través de $B_{B}$. Esto da una matriz real C con

$$
B_A C B_B^{\mathsf T}=X,\qquad |C_{ef}|\le\frac{2M}{h_Ah_B}.\tag{F.3}
$$

También existe una preimagen entera $C_{0}$, sin afirmar una cota de norma: expresamos X como suma de $X_{ab}(e_a-e_{a_0})(e_b-e_{b_0})^{\mathsf T}$, para raíces fijas $a_0,b_0$, y levantamos las dos diferencias mediante caminos en A y B.

Redondeamos C preservando su imagen bilateral. Elegimos un árbol generador de A. Sea P la aplicación que envía un vector de aristas al único vector soportado en ese árbol con la misma incidencia. Así, $B_AP=B_A$ y P se anula en $\ker B_A$. Pongamos

$$
D=C-C_0,\qquad V=PD,\qquad U=D-V.
$$

Entonces $B_AU=0$. Además, $B_A D B_B^{\mathsf T}=0$, por lo que $P(DB_B^{\mathsf T})=0$ y, en consecuencia, $VB_B^{\mathsf T}=0$. Redondeamos cada columna de U como flujo de divergencia cero en A y cada fila de V como flujo de divergencia cero en B. Las matrices enteras resultantes $U_{Z},V_{Z}$ conservan esas identidades y cambian cada entrada en menos de uno. Por tanto, $Z=C_{0}+U_{Z}+V_{Z}$ demuestra (F.2). No se utiliza ninguna cota sobre P. En particular, este argumento no supone que un producto tensorial de matrices de incidencia sea totalmente unimodular.

### F.2. Un expansor de grado acotado para cada tamaño

Para cada $n\ge 1$ existe un grafo simple G sobre n vértices con grado máximo a lo sumo ocho y expansión $h=1/20$. El caso de un vértice es inmediato. Para n mayor, tomamos cuatro permutaciones uniformes independientes y formamos la unión no dirigida de sus aristas de permutación, descartando lazos y repeticiones.

Damos el argumento de conteo con su estimación numérica. Fijemos un conjunto S de tamaño $1\le s\le n/2$ y pongamos $r=\lfloor (s-1)/20\rfloor$. Una permutación con a lo sumo r imágenes que salen de S envía S a $S\cup R$ para algún conjunto R de r elementos fuera de S. Su probabilidad es a lo sumo

$$
\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns.
$$

Por tanto, la probabilidad de que algún conjunto de s elementos falle para las cuatro permutaciones es a lo sumo

$$
U_s=\binom ns\left[\binom nr\binom{s+r}s\big/\binom ns\right]^4.
$$

Verificamos $U_{s}\le 2^{-s}$. Escribimos $A=\binom{n}{r}$, $B=\binom{s+r}{s}$, $\alpha=s/n$ y $x=(s+r)/n$. Como $B\le A$ y $B/\binom{n}{s}\le x^{s}$ (comparando los factores de los dos coeficientes binomiales),

$$
U_s\le A^5x^{3s}.
$$

La estimación elemental $\binom{n}{r}\le (3n/r)^{r}$ para $r\ge 1$ da $A^{20}\le (60/\alpha)^{s}$ cuando $20r\le s$. Una forma de comprobar esta última implicación es utilizar la monotonía de $(60n/t)^{t}$ para $0<t\le n$, en $t=20r$ y $t=s$. El caso $r=0$ da directamente la misma desigualdad. Además,

$$
x^{20}\le(21/20)^{20}\alpha^{20}\le3\alpha^{20}.
$$

Elevar a la potencia veinte la cota para $U_{s}$ da

$$
U_s^{20}\le[60^5\cdot27\cdot\alpha^{55}]^s\le(2^{-20})^s,
$$

porque $\alpha\le 1/2$ y $60^{5}\cdot 27\le 2^{35}$. Sumar $2^{-s}$ en el intervalo finito $1\le s\le \lfloor n/2\rfloor$ da un número estrictamente menor que uno. Por tanto, existe una tupla de permutaciones que sirve para todos esos conjuntos. Para cada S, alguna permutación tiene al menos $r+1\ge s/20$ imágenes salientes. Éstas dan aristas distintas de la frontera simple, incluso tras descartar repeticiones entre permutaciones. Tomar complementos demuestra (F.1) para todos los conjuntos. Cada permutación aporta a lo sumo dos aristas incidentes por vértice, lo que da grado a lo sumo ocho. La desigualdad de corte también implica conexidad.

### F.3. Un relleno con signos acotado en el anfitrión cíclico completo

Sea Q un grafo con tres clases A,B,C, cada una indexada por $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$, y todos los arcos cíclicos entre clases consecutivas. Fijamos una orientación del grafo G de la Sección F.2 sobre el conjunto de índices. Para índices a,b,c, escribimos

$$
t(a,b,c)=[A_aB_b]+[B_bC_c]+[C_cA_a].
$$

Utilizamos las siguientes circulaciones fijas con signos como caras:

1. los $n^{2}$ triángulos latinos t(a,b,a+b);
2. para cada arista orientada $f\to s$ de G y cada a, los dos movimientos

$$
\begin{aligned}m_B(e,a)&=t(a,s,a+f)-t(a,f,a+f),\\m_C(e,a)&=t(a,f-a,s)-t(a,f-a,f);\end{aligned}
$$

3. en cada uno de los tres bloques de clases consecutivas, los rectángulos $(e_s-e_f)(e_{s\prime}-e_{f\prime})^{\mathsf T}$ indexados por dos aristas orientadas de G.

Cada cara es no nula, tiene coeficientes en {-1,0,1} y a lo sumo cuatro arcos no nulos. Los movimientos tienen cuatro arcos, no seis, porque se cancela un lado triangular común. El único cambio de perfil saliente de $m_{B}$ es $e_{s}-e_{f}$ en la clase B; el de $m_{C}$ es $e_{s}-e_{f}$ en la clase C. Cada rectángulo tiene sumas de filas y columnas nulas y, por tanto, perfil saliente cero en cada clase.

Hay a lo sumo $57n^{2}$ caras: G tiene a lo sumo $4n$ aristas, por lo que los tres conteos son $n^{2}$, a lo sumo $8n^{2}$ y a lo sumo $48n^{2}$. Para un arco fijo, las cotas del número de caras incidentes en los cuatro grupos (triángulos, movimientos B, movimientos C y rectángulos) son, respectivamente,

$$
3,\quad32,\quad32,\quad256.\tag{F.4}
$$

Para los movimientos, elegir cuál de sus dos extremos variables coincide con un índice fijo reduce el conteo a las aristas incidentes de G, con a lo sumo cuatro elecciones de este tipo; fijada esta arista, el índice restante queda determinado. Para los rectángulos, elegimos un extremo de cada arista orientada, obteniendo la cota segura $(2\cdot 8)^{2}$. La cota tres para las caras latinas es deliberadamente holgada. Estos conteos siguen siendo válidos si distintas caras indexadas tienen el mismo vector de arcos.

Sea L cualquier subgrafo equilibrado de Q. Denotamos sus grados salientes en las tres clases por $d_{A},d_{B},d_{C}$. Sus sumas coinciden y cada grado es a lo sumo n. Elegimos

$$
z_{ab}=\begin{cases}1,&\text{si el representante de }b-a\pmod n\text{ es }<d_A(a),\\0,&\text{en otro caso.}\end{cases}
$$

La suma de cadenas $z_{ab}$ t(a,b,a+b) tiene el perfil A requerido. Sus errores de perfil B y C tienen suma cero y valor absoluto a lo sumo n. Por la Sección F.1, cada error tiene un flujo entero en G con coeficientes de valor absoluto menor que $20n+1$. Dividimos cada coeficiente en n sumandos enteros de valor absoluto a lo sumo 21. Los utilizamos como coeficientes de $m_{B}(e,a)$ y $m_{C}(e,a)$, respectivamente. Las dos correcciones sólo afectan a sus perfiles respectivos. Obtenemos una circulación con signos Y con exactamente el perfil saliente de L en las tres clases.

Por (F.4), el uso absoluto de caras sobre cualquier arco en esta construcción es a lo sumo

$$
3+2\cdot21\cdot32=1347.
$$

En consecuencia, el residuo $X=1_{L}-Y$ tiene entradas acotadas por 1348. Todos sus perfiles salientes se anulan. Al ser una circulación, sus perfiles entrantes también se anulan. Cada matriz de clases consecutivas tiene, por tanto, filas y columnas de suma cero. Aplicamos (F.2) a cada una de estas tres matrices con ambas constantes de expansión iguales a 1/20. Los coeficientes de rectángulos son enteros de valor absoluto menor que

$$
2\cdot1348\cdot20^2+2=1078402,
$$

y, por tanto, a lo sumo 1078401. Combinando esto con (F.4), obtenemos un relleno con signos de $1_{L}$ cuyo uso absoluto total sobre cada arco es a lo sumo el entero fijo

$$
T=3+2\cdot21\cdot32+1078401\cdot256.\tag{F.5}
$$

Las caras y T se fijaron antes de L. Los coeficientes del relleno dependen de L.

### F.4. Convertir rellenos con signos en un catálogo positivo

Fijemos D subconjunto de Q. Para cada arco $e=u\to v$ de Q, introducimos T caminos positivos de u a v de longitud cuatro y T caminos negativos de v a u de longitud cinco, todos con vértices internos privados. Los caminos distintos tienen vértices internos y arcos distintos. Sus longitudes tienen los residuos apropiados módulo tres, por lo que todos son cíclicos. Sea R su unión, disjunta de D.

El catálogo consta de tres tipos de piezas positivas equilibradas:

- para cada cara, cada signo y cada elección de un canal sobre cada uno de sus arcos no nulos, sustituimos cada arco con signo por un camino en su dirección indicada;
- para cada arco de Q, la unión de cualquier canal positivo con cualquier canal negativo;
- para cada e en D, e junto con el canal negativo de índice cero de e.

Sustituir una circulación entera por caminos dirigidos preserva el equilibrio. Cada pieza enumerada es no vacía y contiene a lo sumo 20 arcos. En particular, no se afirma que el primer tipo sea un único ciclo dirigido; el equilibrio es la propiedad utilizada por la construcción posterior.

Demostramos cobertura exacta, no sólo cobertura de L. Dado L equilibrado subconjunto de D, tomamos el relleno de la Sección F.3 y expandimos sus coeficientes en apariciones unitarias con signos. En un arco e, sean $p_{e},n_{e}$ sus conteos positivos y negativos. Entonces

$$
p_e-n_e=\mathbf1_L(e),\qquad p_e+n_e\le T.
$$

Para e en L, seleccionamos primero la pieza del tercer tipo que utiliza el canal negativo cero. Asignamos canales positivos distintos a las $p_{e}$ apariciones positivas y canales negativos restantes distintos a las $n_{e}$ apariciones negativas. Hay espacio suficiente, pues $n_{e}+1_{L}(e)=p_{e}\le T$. Tanto los canales positivos como los negativos no asignados son $T-p_{e}$, por lo que los emparejamos y seleccionamos las piezas del segundo tipo. Las piezas del primer tipo realizan las apariciones de caras con signo. Cada arco de $R\cup L$ se utiliza ahora exactamente una vez. Las piezas así seleccionadas son distintas, pues son no vacías y disjuntas en arcos. Forman, por tanto, un subconjunto del catálogo fijo, no un multiconjunto que requiera copias adicionales de un arco físico.

El catálogo tiene tamaño a lo sumo $C_{\rm card}n^2$ y carga por vértice a lo sumo $C_{\rm load}n$, donde las constantes congeladas son

$$
\begin{aligned}C_{\rm card}&=114T^4+9T^2+9,\\C_{\rm load}&=(646T^4+T^2+1)(120T+22),\\C_d&=C_{\rm card}+C_{\rm load}.\end{aligned}\tag{F.6}
$$

Para la primera estimación hay a lo sumo $2\cdot 57n^{2}\cdot T^{4}$ piezas de caras, $9n^{2}\cdot T^{2}$ piezas de canales emparejados y $9n^{2}$ piezas de entrada. Las cotas $9n^{2}$ cuentan todos los pares ordenados, por lo que sobreestiman de forma segura los arcos de Q.

Para la estimación de carga, un arco físico pertenece a lo sumo a $2\cdot 323\cdot T^{4}+T^{2}+1$ piezas del catálogo. Un vértice base incide con a lo sumo $6n$ arcos de referencia. Contar a lo sumo cinco arcos por canal y permitir una ficha de canal adicional para un vértice privado da a lo sumo

$$
2[5(2T\cdot6n+1)+6n]\le(120T+22)n.
$$

arcos físicos incidentes, para $n\ge 1$. Contar dos veces los pares (pieza, arco incidente) demuestra (F.6). Estas cotas deliberadamente holgadas cubren tanto los vértices base como los privados. Cualquier digrafo cíclico D sobre N vértices se inserta en Q con N índices por clase; añadir vértices preserva los originales. La fórmula (F.6) da una reserva y un catálogo fijos con número de piezas $\le C_dN^2$ y carga $\le C_dN$. Para $N=0$ usamos la reserva y el catálogo vacíos. Esto demuestra la construcción densa con piezas de tamaño veinte; no es una hipótesis adicional.

### F.5. Reducir una entrada de grado diecisiete a carga de orden raíz cuadrada

Sea Y cíclico con $d_{Y}(v)\le 17$ y $m=|Y|>0$. Pongamos

$$
s=\lfloor\sqrt{2m}\rfloor+1,\quad M=307+290s,\quad A_0=9\cdot597^2\cdot8.\tag{F.7}
$$

Asignamos el soporte de Y a M grupos de cada color, cada uno con a lo sumo s vértices, de modo que arcos distintos de Y tengan pares ordenados de grupos distintos. Procesamos los vértices uno a uno. Además de la capacidad de los grupos, mantenemos que los vértices a distancia no dirigida a lo sumo dos reciben índices de grupo diferentes. En un vértice nuevo, los índices de grupo prohibidos están acotados por:

- $17+17^{2}=306$ por vértices a distancia a lo sumo dos;
- $17^2s=289s$ por arcos existentes cuyo par de grupos coincidiría con el de un arco hacia un vecino procesado anteriormente;
- a lo sumo s-1 grupos llenos, pues el soporte procesado tiene tamaño menor que $s^{2}$.

Para el segundo conteo, un grupo contiene a lo sumo s vértices antiguos, cada uno incidente con a lo sumo diecisiete arcos; hay a lo sumo diecisiete vecinos pertinentes. Los arcos nuevos distintos no pueden coincidir entre sí porque sus extremos antiguos tienen índices de grupo diferentes. Tampoco pueden coincidir las orientaciones opuestas en el vértice nuevo: los colores de sus extremos son distintos. Como M supera la suma de las tres exclusiones, siempre queda un grupo disponible. Esto establece la asignación afirmada, en lugar de limitarse a suponer un cociente simple.

Sea p(v) el grupo de v y sea D el cociente cíclico, con un centro por grupo. La aplicación e->(p(tail e),p(head e)) es inyectiva. Hay $N=3M$ centros y a lo sumo $17s$ arcos de entrada incidentes con cada centro. Como $s^{2}\le 8m$ y $M\le 597s$,

$$
N^2\le A_0m,\qquad(\text{incidencia del centro})^2\le A_0m.\tag{F.8}
$$

Aplicamos la Sección F.4 a D. Para cada arco original $e=u\to v$ introducimos cinco vértices privados y los siguientes caminos:

$$
\begin{aligned}P_e&:v\to x_0\to u,\\O_e&:u\to x_1\to x_2\to p(u),\\I_e&:p(v)\to x_3\to x_4\to v,\\Q_e&:p(u)\to p(v).\end{aligned}
$$

Los colores de p(u),p(v) son los de u,v. Por tanto, los caminos indicados son cíclicos. El ciclo base $P_{e}+O_{e}+Q_{e}+I_{e}$ tiene longitud nueve. La reserva consta de todos estos ciclos base y de la reserva densa sobre los centros. Su catálogo contiene el catálogo denso y:

- el triángulo $e+P_{e}$, para cada e en Y;
- el ciclo base de longitud nueve para cada e;
- $I_{e}+O_{f}$, un ciclo de longitud seis, siempre que $head(e)=tail(f)$.

Dado L equilibrado subconjunto de Y, seleccionamos el ciclo base para cada e fuera de L y el triángulo para cada e en L. En cada vértice antiguo emparejamos sus arcos entrantes de L con sus arcos salientes de L y utilizamos los ciclos de seis correspondientes. Los arcos restantes son exactamente la reserva densa más Q(L). Este último es equilibrado, pues la aplicación de grupos preserva las sumas de divergencias, y es un subgrafo de D por inyectividad. La Sección F.4 particiona este resto. Todas las selecciones son disjuntas en arcos y todas las piezas pertenecen al catálogo fijado antes de L.

Hay a lo sumo $17m$ pares ordenados compatibles (e,f), por lo que el tamaño total del catálogo es a lo sumo (19+C_d A_0)m. El siguiente cálculo de carga registra la cota más fuerte que necesitaremos para los vértices que se identificarán. En un vértice w, sea $S_{w}$ la suma de sus grados en todos los ciclos base de nueve. Los triángulos contribuyen a lo sumo $S_{w}+d_{Y}(w)$, los ciclos base a lo sumo $S_{w}$ y los ciclos de seis a lo sumo $34S_{w}$: un arco puede ser el primer o segundo miembro de a lo sumo diecisiete pares. El catálogo denso contribuye a lo sumo $C_{d}$ N y no contiene vértices antiguos. En particular, $S_{v}=2d_{Y}(v)$ en un vértice antiguo y, por tanto,

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73d_Y(v)\quad\text{para cada vértice antiguo}.\tag{F.9}
$$

En un vértice general, sea ell su incidencia como centro si es un centro, y cero en otro caso. El número de ciclos base que lo contienen es a lo sumo 17+ell, lo que da

$$
\operatorname{load}(w)\le1241+(72+C_d)(\ell+N).
$$

Por (F.8), $(\ell+N)^2\le(2A_0)^2m$. Como $m\ge 1$, la constante congelada

$$
C_m=19+C_dA_0+1241+(72+C_d)(2A_0).\tag{F.10}
$$

acota, por tanto, el tamaño del catálogo por $C_{m}$ m y da $\operatorname{load}(w)^2\le C_m^2m$ en cada vértice. Cada pieza tiene tamaño a lo sumo veinte. Para $m=0$, el catálogo vacío satisface las mismas afirmaciones. La distinción entre (F.9) y la cota de orden raíz cuadrada es esencial: una cota de orden raíz cuadrada por puerto sería insuficiente tras asignar muchos puertos a una misma raíz física.

### F.6. Una red fija de ocho permutaciones en cada raíz

Para cada conjunto finito P existen ocho permutaciones tales que, para todo S subconjunto de P, el número total de canales dirigidos de permutación que salen de S, contados con sus etiquetas de permutación, es al menos

$$
\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.\tag{F.11}
$$

Aquí los canales paralelos se conservan como canales distintos; no es el grafo simple de la Sección F.2. Para $|P|\le 1$ la afirmación es inmediata. Sea $n=|P|$ y fijemos S con $1\le s\le n/2$, $p=s/n$. Para una permutación uniforme, sea I el número de imágenes de S que permanecen en S. Sus momentos factoriales satisfacen

$$
\mathbb E\binom Ik=\frac{\binom sk^2}{\binom nk}\le\binom skp^k.
$$

Así, E $\lambda^{I}$ $\le (1+p(\lambda-1))^{s}$ para $\lambda\ge 1$. Si ocho permutaciones independientes tienen menos de s canales salientes, su conteo interno total supera $7s$. La desigualdad de Markov con $\lambda=4/p$, seguida de $\binom{n}{s}\le (3/p)^{s}$, acota la probabilidad de un conjunto de s elementos que falle por

$$
\left[3(5-p)^8p^6/4^7\right]^s\le2^{-s}.
$$

Para la última desigualdad, $p^{3}(5-p)^{4}$ es creciente para $0<p\le 1/2$ y es menor que 52 en ese intervalo, mientras que $3\cdot 52^{2}<4^{7}/2$. La suma sobre s es estrictamente menor que uno. Por tanto, alguna tupla sirve para todos los conjuntos pequeños. El conteo saliente a través de un corte coincide con el de su complemento para cada permutación, lo que demuestra (F.11).

Descartamos los puntos fijos y damos capacidad unitaria a cada canal restante. Los grados de entrada y salida son ambos a lo sumo ocho. Si los enteros $b_{p}$ satisfacen $|b_{p}|\le 1$ y suman $b_{p}=0$, entonces

$$
\left|\sum_{p\in S}b_p\right|\le\min\{|S|,|P\setminus S|\}.
$$

Por (F.11), se cumplen todas las condiciones de corte dirigido para encaminar este desequilibrio. Por tanto, un flujo entero de capacidad unitaria selecciona canales con la divergencia requerida. Esta última afirmación también se deduce directamente añadiendo una fuente y un sumidero para las demandas positivas y negativas y aumentando el flujo por caminos residuales: si el aumento se detiene antes de encaminar toda la demanda, el conjunto alcanzable desde la fuente viola precisamente una de estas desigualdades de corte. Las capacidades enteras mantienen cada canal seleccionado con valor cero o uno. La red sirve para todos esos b; no se elige después de conocer b.

### F.7. Puertos de raíces y catálogo completo

Sea X un digrafo cíclico arbitrario y pongamos $x=|X|$. Dividimos cada arco de entrada en dos puertos distintos, uno asignado a su raíz de origen y otro a su raíz de destino. La entrada levantada es un emparejamiento sobre $2x$ puertos. Un puerto conserva el color de su raíz. En cada raíz aplicamos la Sección F.6 a su conjunto de puertos. Sustituimos cada canal de la red elegida por un camino privado de longitud tres cuyos extremos son sus puertos. Los extremos tienen el mismo color, por lo que el camino es cíclico. Sea N la unión de todos los caminos de red e I la entrada levantada.

Cada puerto tiene grado total de red a lo sumo dieciséis, cada vértice interno de red tiene grado dos y el emparejamiento levantado añade a lo sumo uno. Por tanto,

$$
\max_v d_{N\cup I}(v)\le17,\qquad |N\cup I|\le49x.\tag{F.12}
$$

En efecto, hay a lo sumo ocho canales por puerto, cada uno con tres arcos, de modo que $|N|\le 24\cdot (2x)$. Las redes quedan fijadas para X. Si L subconjunto de X es equilibrado, su levantamiento tiene divergencia en {-1,0,1} en cada puerto y la suma de divergencias en cada fibra de raíz es cero. La Sección F.6 selecciona canales completos cuyos caminos A cancelan esas divergencias. Así, A unión I(L) es equilibrado, con A subconjunto de N.

Aplicamos una vez la Sección F.5 a $Y=N\cup I$, obteniendo una reserva R disjunta de Y y su catálogo fijo. Ampliamos este catálogo con cada camino individual de canal de N. Dado L, usamos primero la partición mesoscópica para A unión I(L). Después añadimos los caminos individuales de canal no seleccionados en A. Esto particiona

$$
R\cup N\cup I(L).\tag{F.13}
$$

exactamente, utilizando un subconjunto del catálogo fijo ampliado.

Un camino de canal individual añadido no es equilibrado sobre el conjunto de puertos divididos. Sus dos extremos pertenecen a la misma raíz. Tras identificarlos con esa raíz, sus contribuciones entrante y saliente se cancelan. Todas las demás piezas ya eran equilibradas. La inserción física debe preservar arcos distintos; ese paso separado de la Sección 8 no se sustituye por un cociente arbitrario del grafo abstracto. Bajo una realización inyectiva en arcos, el equilibrio desciende sumando divergencias sobre las fibras, y las particiones de (F.13) también descienden.

Hay a lo sumo $16x$ piezas adicionales de canales. Su carga en un vértice antiguo es a lo sumo su grado de red, pues los caminos son disjuntos en arcos. Las ecuaciones (F.9) y (F.12) dan, por tanto, la cota uniforme en vértices antiguos

$$
\operatorname{load}(v)\le73\cdot17+16=1257.\tag{F.14}
$$

Para un vértice mesoscópico realmente nuevo u no hay piezas adicionales de canales, por lo que $load(u)^{2}\le C_{m}^{2}\cdot 49x$. Las cotas restantes son

$$
\begin{aligned}|\mathcal C|&\le(49C_m+16)x,\\\sum_{P\in\mathcal C}|P|&\le(980C_m+48)x.\end{aligned}\tag{F.15}
$$

y cada pieza tiene a lo sumo veinte arcos. La segunda cota mantiene separados los tamaños veinte y tres; no es necesario sustituir ambos por veinte.

Hay exactamente $d_{X}(r)$ puertos asignados a una raíz física r. La precarga total del catálogo transportada por esos puertos es, por tanto, a lo sumo

$$
1257d_X(r).\tag{F.16}
$$

y no 1257 veces el número total de arcos de entrada. Los vértices internos de red no están fijados a r. Éste es el presupuesto de raíces que utiliza la inserción física ponderada. Tomar L vacío en (F.13) también demuestra que el soporte del catálogo contiene R unión N, condición necesaria al definir sus pesos de arcos.

Las ecuaciones (F.12)–(F.16) completan la construcción del catálogo abstracto. Junto con una realización física inyectiva en arcos y el absorbedor terminal demostrado en el Apéndice A, proporcionan la entrada abstracta necesaria para la construcción de familias con leyes de conservación. Esta afirmación se refiere a esa entrada; las pruebas separadas PAR/BAL y semidensa se desarrollan en los Apéndices E y C, respectivamente.

### F.8. Por qué las piezas satisfacen las condiciones terminales de divisibilidad

Para el núcleo de tres colores, el único tipo triangular es 012. En un vértice de color i de una pieza cíclica equilibrada P, los números de vecinos de colores i-1 e i+1 coinciden: son sus grados entrante y saliente. Su perfil local es, por tanto, un múltiplo entero del perfil de esquina de 012. Sumar el equilibrio sobre cada clase de color también muestra que los números de arcos en los tres bloques de clases consecutivas coinciden. En consecuencia, el vector global de conteos de aristas es un múltiplo entero de (1,1,1). Así, P satisface ambas condiciones de divisibilidad entera; el argumento no se basa sólo en la divisibilidad del número total de aristas.

Tras la sustitución física de este artículo, vale el mismo razonamiento porque cada pieza es equilibrada y cíclica, incluidos los canales adicionales cuyos extremos se identificaron con su raíz común. Cada pieza tiene a lo sumo ochenta aristas físicas. Por tanto, el resultado de certificados enteros acotados del Apéndice A puede utilizarse con la cota única de tamaño ochenta. Su certificado se construye en el anfitrión completo permitido; no debe afirmarse que todos sus triángulos auxiliares pertenecen ya al anfitrión incompleto. En su lugar, la construcción terminal se inserta mediante extensión. Su grafo no tiene aristas entre dos raíces antiguas y su construcción ordena los vértices nuevos con a lo sumo cuatro vecinos expuestos previamente, como se demuestra en el Apéndice A. Las desigualdades de disponibilidad y evitación de ese apéndice son las condiciones utilizadas para esta inserción.

Finalmente, aplicamos el lema de ensamblaje de catálogo fijo al catálogo físico. Sus entradas son el número de piezas y la carga de todo el catálogo, no la carga de una selección residual concreta. Las construcciones terminales y sus inserciones físicas se fijan para todas las piezas antes de seleccionar L. La partición para L elige entonces una de las dos descomposiciones de cada construcción ya insertada. Esto explica exactamente dónde intervienen (F.15), (F.16) y la estimación de carga física; no introduce un absorbedor nuevo dependiente de L. La elección cuantitativa de las escalas del anfitrión sigue siendo la de la construcción congelada y del lema de realización física de la Sección 8.
